assumptions: subscription: assumed 4.0 orders per customer over ~6 months.
Margin not given; assumed 50% (typical for beverages) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $160 x 50% x 4.0 orders = $320.00.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $1.20 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.24, relative fit x1.40; 0.0533 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $0.84 (cap $1.20)
score 0.21, relative fit x1.29; 0.0536 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $0.77 (cap $1.10)

score 0.17, relative fit x1.17; 0.0537 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $0.70 (cap $1.01); host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands, otherwise this budget reflows to the other hosts

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $1.20 cap (category default).
